cards.q: In a database table, what is a field?
cards.right: A column: one fact for every record
wrong: A row: all the data about one item
A value that must be unique
cards.why: A field is a column: the same kind of fact (like title) stored for every record. A row is a record.
cards.hook: Field = column (down). Record = row (across).

cards.q: In a database table, what is a record?
cards.right: A row of fields about one item
wrong: A column of one kind of data
A single value in a cell
cards.why: A record is one row: all the related fields about one item, such as one book or one student.
cards.hook: One record = one thing (one book, one dog, one student).

cards.q: What must be true of the values in a primary key field?
cards.why: A primary key picks out exactly one record, so no two records can share its value (and it can't be blank).
cards.hook: Primary key: one value, one record, never repeated.
keys: no two records can share its value

cards.q: What is a foreign key?
cards.right: A field holding another table's key
wrong: A key unique within its own table
A key made from two fields
A password that locks a table
cards.why: A foreign key is a field in one table that holds the primary key of another table, linking the two.
cards.hook: Foreign key = someone else's primary key.
keys: holds the primary key of another table

cards.q: Which data type suits a book's number of pages, such as 96?
cards.why: A count of pages is a whole number with no decimal part, so it is an Integer.
cards.hook: Whole number: Integer. Decimal point: Real.

cards.q: Which data type suits a price such as 4.99?
cards.why: A price has a decimal part, so it is a Real (a floating-point number), not an Integer.
cards.hook: A point in the number? Real.

cards.q: Which data type suits a phone number such as 087 123 4567?
cards.why: It has a leading 0 and spaces and you never do sums with it, so it is stored as text: a String.
cards.hook: If you'd never add it up, store it as a String.

cards.q: A field paid is always either true or false. Which data type is it?
cards.why: A Boolean holds one of only two values: true or false (yes or no).
cards.hook: Two values only: Boolean.

cards.q: STUDENTS has the fields student_id, name and class. Which is the best primary key?
cards.why: Two students can share a name, and many share a class; student_id is given to each student once, so it is unique.
cards.hook: Look for the ID: it was made to be unique.

cards.q: ORDERS (order_id, customer_id, date) and CUSTOMERS (customer_id, name). Which field in ORDERS is a foreign key?
cards.why: customer_id is the primary key of CUSTOMERS; stored in ORDERS it links each order to its customer, so it is a foreign key.
cards.hook: In a table, the other table's ID is the foreign key.
keys: links each order to its customer

cards.q: What does SQL stand for?
cards.why: SQL is Structured Query Language: the language used to query (ask questions of) a relational database.
cards.hook: SQL asks the database questions: a Query Language.

cards.q: In an SQL query, which keyword chooses the columns to show?
cards.why: SELECT names the columns to show, FROM names the table and WHERE filters the rows.
cards.hook: SELECT columns FROM table WHERE condition.

cards.q: In an SQL query, which keyword filters the rows?
cards.why: WHERE gives the condition a row must meet to be in the result; SELECT only chooses the columns.
cards.hook: WHERE picks rows; SELECT picks columns.

cards.q: BOOKS has years 1957, 1960, 1954 and 1957. How many rows does SELECT title FROM BOOKS WHERE year = 1957 return?
cards.why: Only rows whose year equals 1957 are returned: books 1 and 4, so 2 rows.
cards.hook: WHERE keeps only the rows that match exactly.

cards.q: Costs are 6.95, 8.95, 10.00 and 9.95. How many rows does SELECT title FROM BOOKS WHERE cost < 9 return?
cards.why: Only 6.95 and 8.95 are less than 9; 9.95 and 10.00 are more, so 2 rows.
cards.hook: Check each value against the condition, one row at a time.

cards.q: Which SQL query lists every column of every row in BOOKS?
cards.why: The * after SELECT means every column, and FROM BOOKS names the table; with no WHERE, every row comes back.
cards.hook: SELECT * = all the columns.

cards.q: Which SQL query lists BOOKS sorted by year?
cards.right: SELECT * FROM BOOKS ORDER BY year
cards.why: ORDER BY sorts the result by a column (lowest first; add DESC for highest first). WHERE filters, it does not sort.
cards.hook: Sort with ORDER BY, filter with WHERE.

cards.q: What is data redundancy?
cards.right: The same data stored more than once
wrong: Data that is no longer needed
A backup copy of the database
Data in the wrong data type
cards.why: Redundant data is the same value stored in more than one place, like a customer's address on every one of their orders.
cards.hook: Redundant = repeated.
keys: stored in more than one place

cards.q: A customer's address is stored on all 12 of their orders. They move and only 11 are updated. What problem is this?
cards.why: Redundancy led to inconsistency: the copies of one fact now disagree. Storing the address once in CUSTOMERS avoids it.
cards.hook: Store a fact once and it can't disagree with itself.
keys: the copies of one fact now disagree

cards.q: One field holds the dates 02/03/1904 and March 2, 1904. What kind of problem is this?
cards.why: The same kind of data is written in two different formats, so it is inconsistent; one format should be used throughout.
cards.hook: Same data, two looks: inconsistent.

cards.q: One teacher teaches many classes. Where should the foreign key go?
cards.why: The foreign key goes on the "many" side: each class stores its one teacher's teacher_id. A teacher can't store many class_ids in one field.
cards.hook: One-to-many: the "many" table holds the foreign key.

cards.q: What is the first stage of a data analytics project?
cards.why: A project starts with a hypothesis, then collects and cleans the data, analyses it and accepts or rejects the hypothesis.
cards.hook: Guess first, then test: hypothesis, data, clean, analyse.

cards.q: Which of these is a hypothesis?
cards.why: A hypothesis is a statement the data can show to be true or false. A question or an instruction is not a hypothesis.
cards.hook: A hypothesis is a statement, not a question.

cards.q: Members' ages are 12, 15, 14, 140 and 13. What is 140?
cards.why: 140 is far from the other values (probably a typing slip for 14). Cleaning investigates it and corrects or removes it.
cards.hook: Far from the rest? An outlier: check it, then fix or remove.

cards.q: What does data cleaning do?
cards.right: Finds and fixes errors before analysis
wrong: Makes a backup of the data
cards.why: Cleaning finds errors (missing values, duplicates, bad formats, outliers) and fixes or removes them so the analysis can be trusted.
cards.hook: Clean data in, trustworthy results out.

cards.q: A member_name cell is empty. What does data cleaning do with this missing value?
cards.right: Fill it in or remove the record
cards.why: A missing value is filled in with the right or a suitable value, or the record is removed if it can't be fixed.
cards.hook: Missing: fill in or remove. Formats: standardise.

cards.q: LOANS has member_id 3 and MEMBERS lists 3 as Chloe. Which field links a loan to the member's name?
cards.why: member_id is in both tables: the primary key of MEMBERS and a foreign key in LOANS, so 3 in a loan finds Chloe.
cards.hook: Follow the shared key from one table to the other.
